title: Differential Calculus: Optimisation and Rates of Change
seo_title: Grade 12 Optimisation and Rates of Change Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Solve practical problems concerning optimisation and rate of change, including calculus of motion.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 12 calculus worksheets: optimisation, maximum area, volume and profit, velocity, acceleration and rates of change. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Write the quantity to maximise or minimise as a function of one variable.
  • Set the derivative equal to 0 and solve.
  • Check that the answer makes sense (a length must be positive).
  • Velocity is s′(t); acceleration is v′(t) = s″(t). The rate of change at an instant is the derivative.

Examples

Example

A = x(40 − x)

A′ = 40 − 2x = 0

Answer: x = 20, A = 400

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
x or the maximumAnswer the question asked.
s or s′Velocity is the derivative.
Average rateUse the derivative at that instant.

items.q: A farmer has 240 m of fencing for a rectangular kraal. What is the largest area he can enclose?
items.e: Width x, length 240/2 − x. A = x(120 − x); A′ = 120 − 2x = 0 gives x = 60. The kraal is a square: A = 3 600 m².

items.q: Squares of side x cm are cut from the corners of a 30 cm by 30 cm sheet, and the sides are folded up to make an open box. Which value of x gives the largest volume?
items.e: V = x(30 − 2x)². V′ = (30 − 2x)(30 − 6x) = 0, so x = 5 (x = 15 gives no box). The volume is 2 000 cm³.
